blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — iron-status monitoring during epoetin alfa therapy
stem: A client with chronic kidney disease-related anemia is prescribed epoetin alfa (Epogen). Which action is essential before and during therapy?

options.A: Evaluate iron status before and during treatment and maintain iron repletion because iron deficiency can limit the hemoglobin response to epoetin alfa.
options.B: Stop assessing iron status after epoetin alfa begins because the medication supplies the iron needed for new red-blood-cell production during therapy.
options.C: Assess iron status only when oral iron is prescribed because supplemental or intravenous iron needs do not affect the erythropoietic response to epoetin alfa.
options.D: Avoid correcting iron deficiency during epoetin alfa treatment because restoring iron stores reduces the effectiveness of erythropoiesis-stimulating therapy.

rationale: Current EPOGEN labeling directs clinicians to evaluate iron status before and during treatment and maintain iron repletion. Supplemental iron is recommended when ferritin is below 100 mcg/L or transferrin saturation is below 20%, and most CKD patients require supplemental iron during ESA therapy. Iron deficiency is also a recognized cause of inadequate hemoglobin response. Therefore A is correct; B, C, and D contradict the label.
educational_objective: Maintain adequate iron stores during epoetin alfa therapy because iron deficiency can impair the erythropoietic response.
source_document_title: EPOGEN (epoetin alfa) injection — Full Prescribing Information
source_version_date: Current DailyMed label published 2026; label content dated December 31, 2024; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: §2.1 Evaluation of Iron Stores and Nutritional Factors: evaluate iron status before and during treatment; maintain iron repletion; supplemental iron when ferritin <100 mcg/L or TSAT <20%. §5.5: evaluate iron deficiency when hemoglobin response is inadequate.
source_claim_supported: Iron status must be evaluated before and during epoetin alfa therapy and iron repletion maintained; iron deficiency can cause inadequate response.
